newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woolworths to find petrol hard in city - Ampol.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woolworths to find petrol hard in city - Ampol.

text.p: Australian supermarkets group Woolworths Ltd will find it difficult to bring retail petrol outlets to city markets, Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (Ampol) managing director Ian Blackburne said on Wednesday.
"Woolworths will continue to develop sites in country areas, but it will be much harder for them to penetrate metropolitan markets," Blackburne told a media and analysts briefing.
The retailer, which announced last year that it planned to get into petrol marketing, is operating five country sites and selling good volumes, Blackburne said.
Ampol stations near the sites had seen a fall in sales with sites closest to Woolworths most affected, he said.
"Where we can we have competed very vigorously with Woolworths," Blackburne said.
Because of current industry regulations there were sites where Ampol had no influence and it was up to the dealer to decide whether or not to compete, he added.
However, Blackburne said margins in metropolitan markets were tighter than in rural areas, while land and construction costs were higher.
"Woolworths will find it harder to make an inroad into these much more competitive markets," he said.
Ampol is jointly owned by Pioneer International Ltd and Caltex Australia Ltd.
Woolworths said earlier this month that another 40 retail petrol sites had been approved and plans for another 100 were on the drawing board.
